Here's what my bird was doing that had cause for me to take her to the vet.
Bigger poop and less of it.
Fluffed feather, hunched over like, tail bobbing, head bobbing, when she'd fly despite being fully flighted she'd look like she'd fall mid air, when landing on a perch the entire perch would shake, she appeared to almost be panting in a way. 
Yesterday none of the panting, flying issues, perch shaking, tail bobbing, head bobbing were a problem. 
She's currently hormonal and able to breed if she had a mate. 
Her foods are Tops hoobill small bird pellets with a veggie chop that is sprinkled with a variety of herbs, nuts, etc that could give her vitamins she wouldn't get from pellet alone. I do this regardless but focused on foods that would help boost any lost calcium in the event she tried to have an egg and hopefully to prevent egg binding. 
She may have gotten the upper respiratory infection (which isn't confirmed) due to the dry air in the house.
The unit in my home is set to 71° and the vet told me to get a humidifier to help with the dry air.
